findings.claim: `tprod_nonneg` does not need `[L.NeBot]`, and requiring it makes the lemma weaker than the lemmas next to it. `one_le_tprod` (whose additive form is `tsum_nonneg`) and `tprod_le_one` take no `NeBot` assumption. They handle `¬ L.NeBot` with `tprod_bot`, which turns `∏'[L]` into `∏ᶠ`. A finprod of nonnegative terms is nonnegative under the `CommMonoidWithZero`/`ZeroLEOneClass`/`PosMulMono` assumptions the lemma already has. As written, a caller with an arbitrary `L` has to supply `L.NeBot` just to get `0 ≤ ∏'[L] x, f x`. One example would be a `tprod` positivity extension modelled on `evalTsum` in this file, which calls `tsum_nonneg` at an arbitrary `$L`. The only reason the binder is there is that `ge_of_tendsto'` needs it.
findings.requested_change:
Remove `[L.NeBot]` from the signature and split on it inside the proof, as `tprod_le_one` does, e.g.
  by_cases h : Multipliable f L
  · by_cases hL : L.NeBot
    · exact le_hasProd_of_le_prod h.hasProd fun s ↦ s.prod_nonneg fun i _ ↦ hf i
    · simp only [tprod_bot hL]
      exact finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf
  · simp [tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable h]

review_notes: Alternatives I looked at: (1) Asking for a `HasProd.nonneg` companion, by analogy with the non-strict pairs `HasProd.one_le`/`one_le_tprod` and `HasProd.le_one`/`tprod_le_one`. I decided against it. A caller who already has `HasProd f a L` can get `0 ≤ a` in one line from the existing `le_hasProd_of_le_prod` (line 36): `le_hasProd_of_le_prod ha fun s ↦ s.prod_nonneg fun i _ ↦ hf i`. It needs exactly the same assumptions (`ClosedIciTopology`, `L.NeBot`) and does not need T2. Nothing in the file would call the companion. The neighbouring strict bound `Multipliable.one_lt_tprod` has no `HasProd` twin either, so the file has no uniform convention. A strict `0 < ∏'` version would need different hypotheses anyway, because a product of positive terms can converge to 0. (2) Replacing `ge_of_tendsto'` with `le_hasProd_of_le_prod` in the proof is cosmetic, so it is not a separate finding; I only used it in the suggested proof. The `NeBot` finding is based on how `one_le_tprod`, `tprod_le_one` and `tprod_le_of_prod_le'` handle the bot case with `tprod_bot` and finprod in this file, and on `evalTsum` calling `tsum_nonneg` at an arbitrary `L`. I have not compiled the suggested proof; it copies the bot-case pattern already used in `tprod_le_one`.
